title: Language Models Predict Empathy Gaps Between Social In-groups and Out-groups
findings: The study found that Large Language Models exhibit a consistent in-group empathy bias for religion, meaning they predict higher emotion intensities when the perceiver and experiencer share the same religious identity compared to when their religious identities differ. This pattern was robust across most tested models and prompt settings. A specific cultural effect was noted for Buddhism, which showed smaller intensity gaps, possibly reflecting its cultural emphasis on compassion.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured the intergroup empathy gap in Large Language Models. Specifically for religion, it tested whether models predict higher emotion intensity for narratives where the model's persona (perceiver) and the person in the story (experiencer) share the same religion (in-group) compared to when they belong to different religions (out-group).
